Example Sentence: 할아버지는 마음씨가 착하고 노래를 잘 불렀어요.
Sentence Translation: The old man was kind-hearted and sang very well.
Etymology: 마음씨 (heart/mindset) + 가 (subject marker) + 착하다 (to be kind/good), Pure Korean

Example Sentence: 할아버지는 그 집에서 하룻밤 자고 가야겠다고 생각하고 집 안으로 들어갔어요.
English Translation: to stay overnight, to spend the night
Sentence Translation: The old man thought he should sleep there for the night and went inside.
Etymology: 하룻밤 (one night) + 자다 (to sleep) + -고 (and) + 가다 (to go), Pure Korean
Traditional Korean rhythmic filler words used in pansori and folk songs to express excitement, Pure Korean

Example Sentence: 대답을 잘못하면 죽을지도 몰라. 정신 차리자.
English Translation: to pull oneself together, to come to one's senses
Sentence Translation: If I answer wrong, I might die. Pull yourself together.
Etymology: 정신 (精神: mind/spirit) + 을 (object marker) + 차리다 (to prepare/recover)

Example Sentence: 방으로 들어온 도깨비들은 욕심쟁이 혹부리 할아버지에게 크게 화를 냈어요.
English Translation: to get angry, to lose one's temper
Sentence Translation: The goblins who entered the room got very angry at the greedy old man.
Etymology: 화 (火: fire/anger) + 를 (object marker) + 내다 (to express/bring out)

Example Sentence: 욕심쟁이 혹부리 할아버지는 부자가 되려고 욕심을 부리다가 혹만 하나 더 가지게 된 거예요.
English Translation: to be greedy, to act greedily
Sentence Translation: By being greedy and trying to become richer, he ended up getting nothing but one more lump.
Etymology: 욕심 (慾心: greed/selfish desire) + 을 (object marker) + 부리다 (to manage/exhibit)
